activities.caption: fill the blanks — the electron wall
activities.name: coDwarfCloze

config.text: Electron degeneracy pressure is %%0%%-independent — an ember can be cold and still rigid. The more massive the dwarf, the %%1%% it is (R ∝ M^(−1/3)); past %%2%% solar masses, no electron pressure can hold.
config.hint: Pauli forbids electrons sharing states; near the limit they go relativistic and the stiffening saturates.

activities.caption: pair each fact with the remnant it describes
activities.name: coRemnantMatch

pairs.left: about a solar mass in an Earth-sized sphere, no fusion
1.4-ish solar masses in a ~20 km ball at nuclear density
detonates at the Chandrasekhar limit as a Type Ia supernova
GW170817's merger forged the gold and platinum

config.why: Your jewellery is neutron-star fallout — r-process nucleosynthesis, confirmed spectroscopically in the 2017 kilonova.

activities.anchor: the star's surface to move radially at all
activities.caption: bet first — what actually pulses
activities.name: coPulsarPredict

choices: the star itself swelling and shrinking at the radio frequency
two narrow radio beams sweeping past Earth as the star spins
an echo of the supernova that created it
config.why: It is a lighthouse, not a heartbeat: the spin (bought from angular momentum at collapse) sweeps the beams, and the surface never moves radially at all.

activities.caption: file the facts down the density ladder
activities.name: coLadderBuckets

config.prompt: The staircase of losing defenses — file each fact:

items.label: Earth-sized sphere, about a solar mass, no fusion
a ~20 km ball at nuclear density ~7 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³
an event horizon at the Schwarzschild radius
the heavier it is, the smaller it gets
GW150914: two holes of 36 and 29 solar masses merging

config.why: Gravity wins in stages — the electron wall, then the neutron wall, then geometry itself.

activities.anchor: a hundred million times tighter than the last
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the Sun's horizon
activities.name: coSchwarzEstimate

config.prompt: The Earth compressed to a black hole would be a marble 9 mm across; the Sun needs compressing by a factor of 200,000. Roughly how many km from centre would the Sun's horizon sit?
config.why: 637,000 km ÷ 200,000 ≈ 3 km — and remarkably, that Newtonian escape-speed argument gives the exact general-relativistic radius.
config.context: Every rung of the density ladder sits about a hundred million times tighter than the last.

activities.anchor: the photon ring visible as predicted
activities.caption: true or false — the evidence chain
activities.name: coEvidenceJudge

statements.s: Sagittarius A* is 4.3 million solar masses, proven by three decades of stellar orbits.
statements.why: Stars whipped around an invisible mass on Keplerian ellipses — Genzel and Ghez, Nobel 2020.

statements.s: LIGO's detections found dozens of heavy stellar-mass black holes electromagnetic astronomy had never seen.
statements.why: GW150914 (2015): two holes of 36 and 29 solar masses merging.

statements.s: X-ray binaries established stellar-mass black holes — Cygnus X-1's invisible companion.
statements.why: Stripping and heating a blue supergiant — the pre-LIGO evidence.

statements.s: The Event Horizon Telescope photographed M87's black hole in 2019 and our own in 2022.
statements.why: The photon ring visible as predicted.
